chunks: When they submitted to the will of God, and (Abraham) laid (his son) down prostrate on his temple,

key_terms.لِلْجَبِينِ: To the temple/forehead (indicating the position for sacrifice)

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'When they submitted' signify in the story of Abraham and Ismail?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse marks the pivotal moment of *al-islām* (complete submission) where both father and son willingly accepted the divine decree, with 'laying him for the forehead' (*tallahu lil-jabīn*) signifying Ismail's prostration and readiness for the slaughter. This event is often linked to the concept of *Iḥtiṭāb* (divine preparation) and foreshadows the ultimate sacrifice of Imam al-Husayn, emphasizing that true submission involves both readiness to act and trust in God's deliverance.
